headline: The Ranch & Cowboy Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet the crew, count cattle and bales, describe animals and gates, ask where tools are, make polite requests, ask for help, and start Ranch & Cowboy Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Say ranch words clearly and greet the crew, the foreman and the owner politely.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent; greetings

words.note: ch sounds like the ch in church.
Spanish a is always 'ah'; v sounds close to b.
A single r is a quick tap of the tongue.
ll sounds like English y: ca-BA-yo.
rr is a strong rolled r: be-SE-rro.
Roll the rr and stress the last syllable: co-RRAL.
j sounds like a strong English h: o-RE-ha.
The written accent marks the stressed syllable: BÁS-cu-la.
For a woman: la vaquera.

words.en: Good morning, my name is Carlos.
Nice to meet you, I'm the new ranch hand.
words.es: Mucho gusto, soy el vaquero nuevo.
words.note: A woman says: soy la vaquera nueva.
Formal: use with the owner, a buyer or someone older.
Informal: fine between coworkers.

lessons.speaking: Greet the foreman at the corral, say your name, say you are the new ranch hand, and ask how they are.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Count cattle and bales, say the time, and give weights, acres and gallons on the ranch.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and pounds, bales, acres, gallons and head of cattle

words.note: Common in Mexico and the US: una paca de pastura, a bale of hay.
Ranchers count cattle by cabezas: 300 cabezas.
Also the name of the Mexican currency.

words.en: We start at 6 in the morning.
words.es: Empezamos a las 6 de la mañana.

words.note: Use son las for 2 o'clock and later; es la 1 for one o'clock.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what time you start, how many bales you need, and how many head of cattle are in the corral.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Describe animals, gates and troughs, and say who people are and where the horses are.
lessons.focus: ser for what something or someone is, estar for its condition or location

words.note: Agrees: la vaca está enferma.
Ranch use for a mean or wild animal, not 'brave'.
estar: a condition that can change.
ser: what the animal is like.

words.en: The horses are in the corral.
words.es: Los caballos están en el corral.
words.note: estar for location.

words.en: I'm a ranch hand and she is the owner.
words.es: Soy vaquero y ella es la dueña.

lessons.speaking: Tell the foreman if the gate is open or closed, which cow is sick, and where the horses are.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what you have, what there is, and what you need or want for ranch chores.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive

words.note: Feminine noun with el: el agua fría.
Also el heno or el zacate, depending on the region.

words.en: There is water in the trough.
I have the rope in the truck.
words.es: Tengo la soga en la troca.

words.en: I need the pliers and the wire.
words.es: Necesito las pinzas y el alambre.

words.note: Informal tú, between coworkers.

words.en: We have to fill the trough today.
words.es: Hay que llenar el bebedero hoy.
words.note: hay que + infinitive: something that must be done.

words.en: We have to put the salt block in the corral.
words.es: Hay que poner el bloque de sal en el corral.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what you have, what you need for the trough, and ask if they want the gloves.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you will do on the ranch, and what you can or can't do.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer, poder

words.note: Standard US ranch word; also la camioneta.
Many US crews also say la traila.

words.en: I'm going to the south pasture.
We're going to fix the fence tomorrow.
words.es: Vamos a arreglar la cerca mañana.

words.en: What do I do with the post?

words.note: Informal tú; with the boss say ¿Puede usted…?

words.en: I can't move the trailer alone.
words.es: No puedo mover el remolque solo.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker where you are going, what you are going to fix, and ask if they can drive the truck.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Talk about daily ranch work: who rides, who checks the cows, and what the animals eat and drink.
lessons.focus: Present tense of regular -ar, -er, -ir verbs: yo, tú, usted, nosotros, ellos

words.note: Often just la silla on the ranch.

words.en: I work on the ranch Monday to Saturday.
words.es: Trabajo en el rancho de lunes a sábado.

words.note: Informal tú form: montas.

words.en: We drive the cattle to the pasture.
words.es: Nosotros arreamos el ganado al potrero.
words.note: arrear: to drive or move cattle.

words.en: You open the gate and I check the cows.
words.es: Usted abre el portón y yo reviso las vacas.

words.en: The cows eat grass in the morning.
words.es: Las vacas comen pasto en la mañana.

words.en: The calves drink water from the trough.
words.es: Los becerros beben agua del bebedero.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what you do every day on the ranch and ask if they ride horses and when the cattle eat.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask who, what, where, when, how many and why about cattle, tools and the crew.
lessons.focus: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: Agrees: ¿cuántas vacas?, ¿cuántos becerros?
Two words for 'why'; porque, one word, means 'because'.
Mexican ranch word; also la marca.

words.en: How many cows are in the corral?
When are we going to brand?
words.note: herrar: to brand cattle; also marcar.

words.en: Which is the gate to the north pasture?
words.es: ¿Cuál es el portón del potrero norte?

lessons.speaking: Ask the foreman who is in charge, where the branding iron is, and how many cows are in the corral.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say no, never, nobody, nothing and not yet, and ask for more, less or another on the ranch.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos, otro

words.note: Spanish uses a double negative: no veo nada.
Never use un before it: otra jeringa, not una otra.

words.en: There is nobody in the barn.
words.es: No hay nadie en el granero.

words.en: I never work alone with the bull.
words.es: Nunca trabajo solo con el toro.

words.en: The calves don't have the vaccine yet.
words.es: Los becerros todavía no tienen la vacuna.

words.en: There is less water in the trough today.
words.es: Hay menos agua en el bebedero hoy.

words.note: Formal usted command.

lessons.speaking: Tell the foreman the calves don't have the vaccine yet, ask for another needle, and say there is less water today.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Ask for help politely and give simple usted commands at the chute, the gate and the barn.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? + infinitive and usted commands for everyday verbs

words.note: Mexican ranch word for the cattle alley leading to the squeeze.
For a woman: la veterinaria.
For a woman: la encargada.

words.en: Can you open the chute, please?

words.note: Usted command; to a crew say cierren.

words.en: Bring the first aid kit, please.

words.note: Use the personal a before a person: al veterinario.

words.en: Hand me the padlock key, please.
words.es: Páseme la llave del candado, por favor.

lessons.speaking: Ask a coworker politely to open the chute, close the gate, and bring the first aid kit.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize ranch words you already know and ask for help when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad and -ente, and survival phrases

words.note: -ción equals English -tion; these words are feminine.
-dad equals English -ty; these words are feminine.
-ente often matches English -ent.

words.en: Can you repeat more slowly, please?
How do you say 'fence' in Spanish?

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker you speak a little Spanish, ask them to repeat more slowly, and ask how to say a ranch word.
